# ISSUE-51 implementation plan

Add a previewable, linted WorkUnit editor for the GitHub and local backends. Editing changes the proposed contract; only the existing approval command can authorize that revision.

**Shape: Involved.** Byte-preserving edits, tracker title updates, and authoritative claim/approval inspection cross the contract, CLI, tracker, and lease packages.

## What we know

- `newIssueCmd` registers create, approve, and lint, but no edit command (`internal/cli/issue.go:173`). Create's actual flags include `--ready`, `--capability`, and `--parent` as well as the seven requested edit flags (`internal/cli/issue.go:91`).
- Lint calls `contract.ParseWorkUnitFromIssue`, which performs gate and schema validation; shape assessment is advisory (`internal/cli/issue.go:134`, `internal/contract/parser.go:30`). Reuse this validation rather than implementing a second ruleset.
- Parsing supports fenced YAML, Markdown sections and aliases, and external file references. Markdown parsing strips comments and normalizes line endings; `FormatIssueMarkdown` regenerates the body and supplies a default gate (`internal/contract/parser.go:34,106,218`). Whole-body parse/format cannot preserve untouched bytes.
- `DigestWorkUnit` hashes the entire parsed WorkUnit, including title (`internal/contract/security.go:10`). Compare parsed contracts, not body hashes, to determine approval impact.
- `Tracker` exposes `UpdateIssueBody` and `Issue.IsEpic`, but no issue-title setter (`internal/tracker/tracker.go`). GitHub body updates are unconditional PATCH requests (`internal/tracker/github.go:406`); local body updates use the existing locked persistence (`internal/tracker/local.go:308`).
- `Manager.GetCurrentState` is read-only and loads authoritative state; missing state is `coordination.ErrNotFound` (`internal/lease/manager.go:241,1616`). Approval refuses an active unexpired claim; acquisition checks task/policy digests (`internal/lease/manager.go:543,741`). Keeping the old approved digest after an edit makes the new revision ineligible without minting approval.
- Authorization currently recognizes a fixed permission list; edits need their own permission in both backends (`internal/tracker/github.go:165`, `internal/tracker/local.go:77`).
- A reusable diff implementation exists, but is private and can omit large diffs (`internal/harness/diff.go:19`). `make check` runs formatting checks, vet, staticcheck, and race tests (`Makefile`).

## What we're assuming

- Implement the seven acceptance-listed mutation flags plus `--dry-run` and `--json`. Preserve parent/capability sections, but do not add their editing or linking semantics. This is the smallest interpretation of “same flags as create”; never expose `--ready`. Check the command help and have plan review confirm this interpretation.
- An external-file WorkUnit cannot have its task sections replaced through a tracker-body-only API without changing its representation or editing repository files. Refuse section edits to that representation with an actionable message; retain the body unchanged. Confirm this boundary with fixtures in step 1 and call it out for review.
- Maintainer-assisted agents invoke the normal authorized CLI; this feature does not add a fork coordinator operation or expose credentials. Reject `--fork` for editing.

## Open questions and review limits

- The criterion saying concurrent web edits are “never” overwritten is stronger than re-read-before-write can guarantee: GitHub's existing unconditional PATCH still has a read/write race. Step 3 will implement and test the required immediate re-read, including title, and document that residual interval here. A true atomic conditional update needs a separately verified GitHub capability or a revised WorkUnit; do not silently claim atomicity or block sandbox implementation on a live service.
- Claims can likewise begin between the final state read and tracker write. Step 3 rechecks immediately before writing; digest fencing rejects later worker mutations once the body changes. Full serialization of claim acquisition with tracker edits is a broader coordination change and requires maintainer review rather than an unfenced state write.
- Confirm YAML source-span handling (multiline scalars, comments, aliases) in step 1. Reject ambiguous input without writing instead of normalizing unrelated text. Plan review should confirm external-reference refusal satisfies the intended format scope; this is a declared coverage boundary, not an omitted criterion.
- Separate title/body/label requests cannot form a GitHub transaction. Step 3 must test partial failures and report exactly which changes succeeded; never automatically restore an old body over possible concurrent edits.

## Design and exact touchpoints

1. **Contract editing:** create `internal/contract/edit.go` and `edit_test.go`, with `WorkUnitEdit` (presence-aware replacement fields) and `EditWorkUnitIssue`. Reuse `ParseWorkUnitFromIssue`, `ValidateWorkUnit`, and `FormatIssueMarkdown` to validate and produce canonical replacement fragments. Operate on offsets into the original body; never serialize the entire parsed WorkUnit. For Markdown, replace only the selected section's content, recognize the parser's aliases, and append a missing selected section. Preserve all other headings, comments, whitespace, line endings, unknown sections, and trailing text exactly. Repeated flags replace the entire list; use Cobra `Changed` to distinguish omission from explicit empty values. Reject ambiguous duplicate target sections. For fenced YAML, follow parser precedence, locate selected top-level field spans using YAML nodes and original source offsets, and replace only those fields using YAML encoding. Preserve fence delimiters, unrelated keys, comments, and surrounding prose. Explicit title updates must also replace an existing YAML title so the parsed digest reflects the requested issue title. Reject unsupported/ambiguous source constructs without writes. Reparse the candidate and ensure it matches the intended field changes, guarding against injected headings or extra YAML fields.
2. **Tracker support:** modify `internal/tracker/tracker.go`, `github.go`, and `local.go` to add a minimal `UpdateIssueTitle` method while retaining `UpdateIssueBody` for body writes. Update interface test doubles as required. Extend both authorization implementations with `edit-task`, using the existing write/collaborator policy without granting approval. Title updates use the existing GitHub endpoint and local locked, safefs-backed persistence. Add backend tests in `github_test.go` and a new `issue_edit_test.go` as appropriate.
3. **CLI orchestration:** register `newIssueEditCmd` in `internal/cli/issue.go`; implement it and a typed preview result in new `internal/cli/issue_edit.go`. Resolve tracker/manager, reject fork mode and Epics, authorize `edit-task`, read issue and authoritative state, and construct the proposed title/body. Treat only missing coordination state as an unapproved draft; propagate storage, permission, and malformed-state errors. Use `GetCurrentState`, never comments or labels, to detect claims and existing approval. Refuse an active unexpired claim with owner, RFC3339 expiry, and `swarm issue release N`; never release another worker's claim. Use old/proposed parsed task digests and recorded approved digest to report unchanged/current/stale approval accurately.

   Produce one preview containing body unified diff, title change, lint result/errors, task digest impact, claim impact, and next command. Dry run prints it without any tracker or authoritative state mutation, including invalid proposals (nonzero exit) and blocked claims (nonzero exit with impact). JSON emits the same information as structured data without mixed prose. For normal edits lint must pass before any write. Immediately before the first write, re-read authoritative claim state and the issue, rejecting changed original body/title, new Epic status, or active claim. No-op title/body edits perform no writes. Persist body through `UpdateIssueBody`, and title through the new method only if changed. If the task digest changes on an issue with recorded approval (including an already stale approved revision), remove `swarm:ready` and add `swarm:draft`, preserving unrelated labels; honor any trusted configured ready-label equivalent from the approved base. Print `swarm issue approve N`. Leave authoritative approval/task/policy fields and artifacts untouched: never copy the proposed digest into approved state or invoke `ApproveTask`. Unchanged task digests preserve all approval state and labels, even when body formatting changes. Propagate write/label errors with partial-success details and recovery instructions; do not report success or perform unsafe rollback.
4. **Diff:** add a small body-diff helper in `internal/cli/issue_edit_diff.go` and tests. Follow the existing unified-diff conventions without widening the harness API. Use an exact whole-body replacement hunk if a bounded contextual diff would exceed its budget; include missing-final-newline markers. The preview must show the complete change rather than a “too large” placeholder.
5. **Regression tests:** add `internal/cli/issue_edit_test.go` using `newCLIFixture` (`internal/cli/cli_test.go:38`), a recording tracker wrapper, controlled clock, and deterministic read hooks/HTTP responses. Cover every row in TEST_PLAN.md, including errors and zero writes. Add lease regressions in `internal/lease/manager_test.go` proving the existing approval accepts unchanged parsed content and rejects a changed contract until separate approval.
6. **Documentation:** update the CLI table at `README.md:231`, add editing/preview/reapproval examples to `docs/developer.md`, and add an Unreleased entry to `CHANGELOG.md`. Explain whole-list replacement, omitted-section preservation, claim release, separate approval, both backends, and the declared format boundary in clear developer prose. Verify examples against implemented help.
7. Run focused tests, required build/test/vet checks, and `make check`. Review the diff for protected-file changes and scope. Do not modify protected harness files, publish, stage coordinator state, or implement beyond this WorkUnit.

## Alternatives considered

- Whole-body parse/format is simpler but breaks byte preservation; use source-span replacement with existing parsing/rendering instead.
- Rewriting approved state to the new digest would approve implicitly; retain the old state so existing digest checks invalidate execution naturally.
- A general edit transaction/reservation protocol could serialize every writer, but exceeds the requested command and cannot serialize GitHub web edits by itself. Keep the required re-read behavior and expose its limit for review.

## Verification environment

This planning checkout has no discoverable Git metadata (`git status --short` reports “not a git repository”), and production files are read-only. Implementation validation needs the normal writable task checkout/CI. No live GitHub or container runtime is required for the planned automated tests; use local fixtures and mocked GitHub HTTP. The planner has not run implementation checks or changed production files.

# ISSUE-51 test plan

Tests below are planned implementation verification, not results from this planning phase. Use temporary repositories and mocked GitHub HTTP, never a live issue. Every refusal must assert title/body/labels and authoritative state are unchanged; count tracker writes, comments, approval calls, and store CAS operations where applicable.

| Acceptance criterion | Concrete cases and evidence | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Seven replacement flags; untouched sections preserved byte for byte | Table-driven `TestEditWorkUnitIssue*` covers each field separately and combined, repeated list flags replacing rather than appending, absent flags, explicit empty values, missing optional sections, aliases, CRLF, comments, custom headings, whitespace, and final newline. Compare every untouched source slice exactly. Cover Markdown and fenced YAML, including embedded title precedence. Malformed/ambiguous targets and external-reference edits refuse without changes. `TestIssueEditFlags` asserts allowed flags, no `--ready` or add/remove flags, one numeric argument, and that omitted workflow/gate do not reset defaults. | `go test ./internal/contract -run TestEditWorkUnitIssue`; `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestIssueEdit(Flags|Replacement|Preservation)'` |
| 2. Same lint rules; invalid edit writes nothing | Compare candidate parse errors to `ParseWorkUnitFromIssue`/`issue lint` for empty objective, empty acceptance, invalid gate/workflow, and parser/schema failures. Test repairing a malformed selected section when the resulting candidate is valid. Test heading/YAML injection that would alter an unselected semantic field. A failure reports lint details and leaves body, title, labels, and state unchanged. | `go test ./internal/cli -run TestIssueEditLint`; `go test ./internal/contract -run TestEditWorkUnitIssue` |
| 3. Dry run shows unified diff, lint, approval/claim impact and has no writes | `TestIssueEditDryRun*`: approved changed task, unchanged digest, draft/no state, invalid candidate, active claim, title-only change, and JSON variants. Snapshot tracker and coordination data and require zero mutation calls. Assert diff hunk ranges, exact added/deleted lines, lint verdict, owner/expiry where relevant, and reapproval command. Diff tests cover multi-hunk output, additions/deletions, missing final newline, unchanged content, and a large exact replacement diff. | `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestIssueEdit(DryRun|Diff)'` |
| 4. Changed digest demotes; unchanged digest preserves approval and labels | Approve fixture through existing manager; edit objective/title/list and assert recorded approved digest remains old, ready removed, draft added, unrelated labels kept, and exact `swarm issue approve N` advice. Test absent approval, stale approval, policy-configured ready label from approved base, exact no-op, and source changes with the same parsed contract. Assert no approval/CAS calls and no artifacts changed. Lease regression proves acquisition/approval verification rejects changed content, accepts unchanged content, and permits changed content only after explicit approval. Inject body/title/label failures and verify truthful partial-success errors and no rollback. | `go test ./internal/cli -run TestIssueEditApproval`; `go test ./internal/lease -run TestIssueEdit` |
| 5. Active unexpired claim refusal | Fixed-clock active claim owned by caller and by another owner; expiry in future refuses normal and dry-run paths with owner, RFC3339 expiry, and release command. Expired, exactly-at-expiry, and released claims do not block. Re-read hook introduces a claim before write and verifies refusal. Corrupt/unreadable state fails closed; missing state alone is allowed. | `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestIssueEdit(Claim|State)'` |
| 6. Re-read detects concurrent body changes | Recording tracker returns body A initially and body B on final read; require conflict and zero mutations. Cover title changes, identical reread, issue becoming Epic, final-read error, and final state-read error. Assert final read precedes the first write. This tests detection before write, not atomic exclusion of a web update between GET and PATCH. | `go test ./internal/cli -run TestIssueEditConcurrent` |
| 7. Epic refusal and both backends | Local typed Epic and mocked GitHub type Epic refuse before parsing/writing. Local integration verifies persisted title/body/labels; GitHub HTTP tests verify fetch/re-fetch, body PATCH through `UpdateIssueBody`, title PATCH, and label changes. Authorization accepts repository write collaborators, rejects unauthorized actors, and fork mode refuses without dispatch. Preserve local safefs/symlink protections. | `go test ./internal/cli -run 'TestIssueEdit(Epic|Backend|Authorization|Fork)'`; `go test ./internal/tracker -run 'Test.*(IssueEdit|UpdateIssueTitle|UpdateIssueBody)'` |
| 8. Required regression coverage and make check | Run all tests above, then full build/test/vet and repository lint/race checks. Existing adversarial tests remain intact. CI/writable implementation checkout supplies normal toolchain/cache access; record environment failures distinctly from code failures. | `go build ./...`; `go test ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `make check` |
| 9. README, developer guide, changelog | Verify CLI table includes edit, developer guide demonstrates replacement/preview/reapproval and both backends, and Unreleased entry describes user behavior. Check all documented edit flags against command help, relative links/anchors, and shell snippets with `bash -n`. Preserve README diagrams/badges and welcoming documentation voice. | `go run ./cmd/swarm issue edit --help`; `go run ./cmd/swarm issue create --help`; run `bash -n` on extracted changed bash snippets and manually resolve changed relative links/anchors. |

Run focused suites once implementation is ready:

```bash
go test ./internal/contract ./internal/tracker ./internal/cli ./internal/lease
go build ./...
go test ./...
go vet ./...
make check
```

Test names above specify new tests to implement. No live GitHub write is needed. Plan review must assess the explicit boundaries in PLAN.md: external-file representation, the flag subset, and the non-atomic read/PATCH interval. Do not claim full concurrent-write serialization from a mocked re-read test.

VERDICT: APPROVED

# ISSUE-51 plan review

The reviewer checked PLAN.md and TEST_PLAN.md against WORKUNIT.md, SYSTEM_PROMPT.md conventions, and protected paths. Every cited code location under **What we know** was opened in the workspace and matches what the plan says.

## Acceptance coverage

| # | Criterion | Plan | Test plan | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | Seven flags, replace named sections, preserve others byte for byte | Step 1 (source-span edits, Markdown + fenced YAML), step 3 | Row 1 | ✅ |
| 2 | Same lint rules before write; refuse invalid with errors, no write | Steps 1, 3 (reuse `ParseWorkUnitFromIssue`) | Row 2 | ✅ |
| 3 | `--dry-run`: unified diff, lint, approval/claim impact, no changes | Steps 3, 4 | Row 3 | ✅ |
| 4 | Digest change → ready→draft + print `swarm issue approve N`; no-op keeps all | Step 3 | Row 4 | ✅ |
| 5 | Refuse an unexpired claim, with owner, expiry, release hint | Step 3 | Row 5 | ✅ |
| 6 | Re-read before write; refuse on body change | Step 3 | Row 6 | ✅ (see note on the remaining race window) |
| 7 | Epic refusal; github + local backends | Steps 2, 3 | Row 7 | ✅ |
| 8 | Required tests; `make check` passes | Steps 5, 7 | Row 8 | ✅ |
| 9 | README table, `docs/developer.md`, CHANGELOG | Step 6 | Row 9 | ✅ |

## Constraints and invariants

| Constraint | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Editing never approves | ✅ No `--ready`. `ApproveTask` is never called, and approved state never gets the new digest. The old digest stays, so `TaskApprovalCurrent` rejects the edited revision. |
| Reuse parse/render/lint and `UpdateIssueBody`; no new body format | ✅ The body is written only through `UpdateIssueBody`. The new `UpdateIssueTitle` is needed for `--title`, writes no body, and does not break this constraint. |
| Flag set ⊆ create flags + `--dry-run`/`--json`; no add/remove flags | ✅ The seven listed flags are a subset. Leaving out `--capability`/`--parent` is allowed because the constraint sets an upper limit, and the acceptance criteria list only the seven. **The reviewer accepts this reading.** |
| Protected paths / `allow_harness_changes: false` | ✅ Every touchpoint is under `internal/`, `README.md`, `docs/developer.md`, or `CHANGELOG.md`. None is protected. |
| Conventions (gofmt, focused packages, table-driven tests) | ✅ The diff helper stays private to the CLI rather than widening the harness API, and tests are table-driven. |

## Shape and rigor

The plan is labeled **Involved**. It names its touchpoints, gives three real alternatives, and separates assumptions from verified facts. That level of rigor fits the shape. Every implementation check can run in the sandbox (local backend, mocked GitHub HTTP). Nothing waits on a live service.

## Rulings on the boundaries the planner asked about

1. **Flag subset:** accepted (see above).
2. **External-file (`swarm-workunit-path`) WorkUnits:** refusing section edits with a clear message is accepted. The body never holds those sections, so editing them through a body-only API would mean adding a new representation, which the constraints forbid. List this boundary in `docs/developer.md`.
3. **Remaining GET→PATCH window:** accepted. The criterion asks for an immediate re-read and refusal, and the plan does that. GitHub's issue PATCH has no conditional-update primitive, so the plan is right not to claim atomicity. State the window in a code comment and in the developer docs. If maintainers want stronger guarantees, open a follow-up WorkUnit.

## Non-blocking recommendations

- **Lint parity:** call exactly `contract.ParseWorkUnitFromIssue(number, title, body)`, as `issue lint` does, rather than the `WithRoot` variant. Then edit and lint can never disagree.
- **Ready label without recorded approval:** if the digest changes and the issue has the ready label but no recorded approval state, say so in the preview instead of silently leaving the label. Behavior can stay as planned; with `RequireReadyLabel`, the label alone never authorizes a claim.
- **`--depends-on` explicit empty:** create uses `IntSliceVar`. Make sure `--depends-on=` (empty) clears the section through `Changed` and doesn't fail to parse, and add one row for it.
- **Fenced-YAML span editing** is the riskiest part. Keep the "refuse when ambiguous" fallback strict, and add the re-parse equality check from step 1 as a single shared guard that runs on both the Markdown and YAML paths.
- **Scope:** the lease regression tests in `internal/lease/manager_test.go` are small and protect the "never approves" invariant, so keep them. Don't add more lease changes than that.

## Suggested follow-up WorkUnits (out of scope here)

- Editing `--capability` / `--parent` relationships with the matching sub-issue link updates.
- Serializing tracker edits with claim acquisition, or using a conditional update if GitHub supports one, to close the remaining race windows.

# Implementation Summary (Issue #51)

## What we learned

- Cobra's pflag integer-slice value rejects an empty token; commands that support clearing a list with `--flag=` need explicit empty-value handling.
